p: Sidmouth isn't a town that rushes, and a single-screen cinema suits it perfectly. There's no agonising over which of twelve films to see; you pick a night, settle into your seat and enjoy it. That gentle pace is a big part of the town's charm, and it's why so many visitors come back year after year.
If you're planning around the weather, a matinee is a great way to rescue a drizzly afternoon, and on a bright day an early evening showing leaves time for the sunset along the front beforehand.

Connaught Gardens, perched above the western end of the esplanade, are lovely for a wander, and Jacob's Ladder, the wooden staircase down to the beach below, is a favourite with children. The Byes, a long riverside walk beside the little River Sid, is a peaceful leg-stretcher that's flat and easy for most people.

Just outside town, The Donkey Sanctuary at Salcombe Regis is a much-loved free day out for families, and further west, Ladram Bay's red sandstone stacks are worth seeing. In early August, Sidmouth Folk Festival fills the town with music and dancing, so expect it to be busier and book anything you can if your trip falls then. A film at The Radway is the perfect quiet full stop to a busy festival day.
Parking in the centre can be tight in high summer, so arriving a little early, or walking in from your accommodation, takes the stress out of making the start time.
